end.summary:
Reviewed states and common uses of non-metals.
Pari correctly identified most listed non-metals as solids or gases; iodine was described as a solid.
Connected graphite with pencils, chlorine with water, iodised salt, and nitrogen with chips packets and fertilisers.
Explained oxygen, carbon and nitrogen roles in living things.
Teach-back was not passed; nitrogen’s role in fertilisers was clarified later in turn 13.
end.parentNote: Asha practised classifying non-metals, linking them to everyday uses, and explaining their importance to living things. Pari used examples and explanations well, including graphite in pencils and nitrogen in chips packets. They initially questioned how nitrogen could be useful in both chips packets and fertilisers, then corrected this by explaining that plants absorb nitrogen compounds from soil and use them to make protein. At home, ask Pari to make a three-column chart of non-metals, their states, and one everyday use.
